achievements-bye.where: Achievements: Dex says goodbye and walks off
achievements-bye.text: They’re kept in this browser, for these pages and the desk alike. Now go earn some!

achievements-card.where: Achievements: Dex points at the first badge
achievements-card.text: Each badge says what to do to earn it. Press one to see more, and where to go for it.

achievements-desk.where: Achievements: Dex points at the The 1994 desk heading
achievements-desk.text: The 1994 desk: switch on the PC, dial a BBS, run the programs on it.

achievements-hearts.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Tin heart badge
achievements-hearts.text: Tin hearts are tucked away inside the games. Touch one and it counts here.

achievements-hello.text: Hi! I’m Dex Dynamo, from the year 2000. This page keeps track of everything you’ve done here.

achievements-making.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Making games heading
achievements-making.text: Making games: start one, change a file, run the Level check, download it for DOS or the web.

achievements-playing.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Playing heading
achievements-playing.text: Playing: finish games on the web, on the 1994 desk, even on a phone held sideways.

achievements-reset.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Reset achievements button
achievements-reset.text: Start over forgets the badges in this browser, after asking. Your games and saves stay.

achievements-site.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Around the site heading
achievements-site.text: Around the site: meet the cast, unfold a map, visit the Library. A few badges stay hidden until you find them.

achievements-summary.where: Achievements: Dex points at the count of achievements unlocked
achievements-summary.text: Up top: how many you’ve unlocked so far, out of all of them.

achievements-watching.where: Achievements: Dex points at the Watching heading
achievements-watching.text: Watching: sit back with a walkthrough, or record a video of the screen.

bbs-busy.where: BBS: Dex points at the modem
bbs-busy.text: The PC is busy right now. Quit what’s running, then click the modem to call the BBS yourself.

bbs-bye.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-bye.text: Back to the menu, G says goodbye, and the modem hangs up. NO CARRIER!

bbs-dial.where: BBS: Dex points at the modem
bbs-dial.text: TERMINAL dials 1-412-555-SAND. Hear that screeching? Two modems, shaking hands.

bbs-done.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-done.text: Downloaded and unzipped into C:\DOWNLOAD. When the tour ends, it comes off again, so your drive stays yours.

bbs-download.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-download.text: D and the number downloads it. At 14,400 bits a second, this would take a few minutes.

bbs-hello.text: Dex Dynamo, dialing in from the future! In 1994 you called a BBS: somebody’s own PC, answering the phone.

bbs-login.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-login.text: Connected! It asks for a handle. GUEST gets in without a password.

bbs-logoff.where: BBS: Dex says goodbye and walks off
bbs-logoff.text: That’s a BBS call. The modem on the desk dials one any time you like.

bbs-menu.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-menu.text: The main menu. The letter N scans the newest files: the Sandbox games, free to download.

bbs-ratio.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-ratio.text: Last few callers, then my rule: upload one file for every five you take. Leeches get deleted!

bbs-speed.where: BBS: Dex presses Unlimited in the modem’s speed menu
bbs-speed.text: Too slow? Change the modem’s speed, even mid-call. Unlimited is today’s speed: no waiting!

bbs-sysop.text: And The Sandbox BBS runs right here, on my PC! I’m its SysOp. Go ahead, Dex, give it a call.

bbs-view.where: BBS: Dex points at the screen
bbs-view.text: V and a file’s number shows its details: what it is, how big, and its author’s notice.

cast-appears.where: Cast: Teddy points at the games Teddy is seen in
cast-appears.text: And the games each one is seen in. Press a picture to go to that game.

cast-bye.where: Cast: Doc Leo says goodbye and walks off
cast-bye.text: Hey, that’s my hat! Thanks for coming to the show, folks.

cast-card.where: Cast: Teddy points at Teddy’s card
cast-card.text: Each regular has a card: who they are, and a little about them. Teddy knows left from right!

cast-families.where: Cast: Teddy points at the three kinds of games
cast-families.text: Three kinds of games: Sandbox Software, the Bard of Bizarre’s songs, and the games from the original CD.

cast-filters.where: Cast: Teddy points at the Show the cast of buttons
cast-filters.text: These show just one kind’s regulars, or everyone.

cast-gwinn.text: It wasn’t me. (It was me.) Zoomies!

cast-hello.text: Smile on: showtime! I’m Doc Leo. This is the cast: everyone from the new games.

cast-next.where: Cast: Teddy presses the Next character button
cast-next.text: The arrows bring on the next one, or the one before.

cast-pick.where: Cast: Teddy points at the Pick a character list
cast-pick.text: Or call one by name from this list.

cast-sound.where: Cast: Teddy points at the stage’s sound button
cast-sound.text: The stage stays quiet until you ask. Then the Teddy games’ theme plays along.

cast-stage.where: Cast: Teddy points at the stage
cast-stage.text: On stage, each regular walks on and says hello, drawn from their own game.

desk-box-disks.where: Desk: Lewie points at the disks in the box
desk-box-disks.text: Inside, the game’s disks. Click them and disk one goes in drive A: to play.

desk-box-extras.where: Desk: Lewie points at the list of what else came in the box
desk-box-extras.text: And everything else that came in the box, each piece ready to read or print.

desk-box-manual.where: Desk: Lewie points at the manual in the box
desk-box-manual.text: Its manual, with a cover all its own.

desk-box-open.where: Desk: Lewie presses the box standing face out
desk-box-open.text: Like this one. Down it comes!

desk-box-turn.where: Desk: Lewie points at the box, turning
desk-box-turn.text: It turns all the way around, so you can read the back. Drag it to turn it yourself, or scroll to zoom.

desk-bye.where: Desk: Lewie says goodbye and walks off
desk-bye.text: That’s my room. Now, who wants to make a game?

desk-clock.where: Desk: Lewie points at the wall clock
desk-clock.text: A giant wristwatch makes a fine wall clock. Turn the lights off and its hands glow.

desk-diskbox.where: Desk: Lewie points at the disk box
desk-diskbox.text: The disk box has a floppy for every game. Pick one and it goes in drive A: and starts.

desk-drive.where: Desk: Lewie points at drive A:
desk-drive.text: That’s drive A:. With a disk in, buttons beside it play it, design it, or open it in today’s web.

desk-enlarge.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Enlarge screen button
desk-enlarge.text: This little button fills the window with the screen. Back to the desk brings the room back.

desk-gmbox.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Game-Maker box
desk-gmbox.text: The Game-Maker box: turn it over, read the Owner’s Guide, or put the CD in and start Game-Maker.

desk-guides.where: Desk: Lewie points at the ? Guides button
desk-guides.text: Press the question mark any time to see this tour again.

desk-hello.text: Hey, I’m Lewie. Welcome to my room! It’s December 1994, and this PC is where the games get made.

desk-keyboard.where: Desk: Lewie points at the keyboard
desk-keyboard.text: Type on your own keyboard, or click the keys here to press them on the PC.

desk-mag-cover.where: Desk: Lewie points at the magazine’s pages
desk-mag-cover.text: The big news on the cover: Game-Maker’s source code, set free!

desk-mag-links.where: Desk: Lewie presses the magazine’s next page arrow
desk-mag-links.text: Its links work, too: they play games, call the BBS, or point out things in my room.

desk-mag-open.where: Desk: Lewie presses the catalog and the magazine
desk-mag-open.text: Let’s peek inside this month’s TURBO BUTTON.

desk-mag-turn.where: Desk: Lewie presses the magazine’s next page arrow
desk-mag-turn.text: Turn the pages with the arrows: reviews, hints, readers’ letters, and ads for the things on this desk.

desk-modem.where: Desk: Lewie points at the modem
desk-modem.text: The modem calls the BBS, where you can download more games. Click its speed to change it.

desk-pad.where: Desk: Lewie points at the game pad
desk-pad.text: The GRAVITAS pad is the PC’s joystick. A real gamepad works too, and a click opens big buttons.

desk-pad-panel.where: Desk: Lewie points at the game pad’s large controls
desk-pad-panel.text: Big buttons for the d-pad’s eight ways and all four buttons. Game-Maker games read the d-pad and the red and yellow buttons.

desk-papers.where: Desk: Lewie points at the catalog and the magazine
desk-papers.text: The shareware catalog and TURBO BUTTON magazine. Read either one; the catalog can even call the BBS.

desk-phone.where: Desk: Lewie points at the wall phone
desk-phone.text: The phone really dials. Try the numbers on Mom’s notes, or call for the time and the weather.

desk-poster.where: Desk: Lewie points at the poster
desk-poster.text: My big plan: shovel snow all winter to buy Game-Maker. Eighty-nine dollars, plus four for shipping!

desk-power.where: Desk: Lewie presses the Power button
desk-power.text: Power switches the PC on. It boots DOS, just like a real one.

desk-screen.where: Desk: Lewie points at the screen
desk-screen.text: Everything runs on this screen: the DOS prompt, Game-Maker, the games, even the BBS.

desk-shelf.where: Desk: Lewie points at the shelf of game boxes
desk-shelf.text: My shelf has a box for every game. Take one down to turn it over, read its manual, or play it.

desk-sticky.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Too retro? sticky note
desk-sticky.text: Too retro? This note takes you to today’s web, with all the same games.

desk-switch.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Desk, DOS and Web switch
desk-switch.text: Desk, DOS and Web switch views. DOS is this same PC, filling the whole window.

desk-turbo.where: Desk: Lewie points at the Turbo button
desk-turbo.text: Turbo runs it at full speed. Switch it off and games crawl along like on an old 286.

dos-bbs.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at BBS in the ⋯ menu
dos-bbs.text: BBS dials the board with the modem. The line speed under it says how fast.

dos-blaster.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at Sound Blaster card in the ⋯ menu
dos-blaster.text: Without the Sound Blaster card, games beep their sounds on the PC speaker.

dos-bye.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks says goodbye and walks off
dos-bye.text: That concludes the tour! Now, if you’ll excuse me, THE CHEZ needs charging.

dos-card.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the registration card
dos-card.text: Or mail the registration card. Once the reply comes, Game-Maker stops asking.

dos-check.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the screen
dos-check.text: Game-Maker may ask for a word from its Owner’s Guide. That was copy protection, back in 1994.

dos-disks.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Disks button
dos-disks.text: Disks is your disk box: Play, Design, or just Insert any game’s floppy in drive A:.

dos-full.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Full screen button
dos-full.text: Full screen hides everything else, the browser too.

dos-gm.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Game-Maker button
dos-gm.text: The Game-Maker button takes you back to it from anywhere, with its CD in drive D:.

dos-guide.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Owner’s Guide beside the screen
dos-guide.text: The guide opens beside it, at the right page, the word marked. Type the word and you’re in.

dos-hello.text: Professor Fiddlesticks, at your service! This is the very same PC, minus the room, filling the window.

dos-keys.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Keys button
dos-keys.text: No keyboard? Keys opens big on-screen keys for the PC.

dos-links.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Links button
dos-links.text: Links lists addresses that open this page on a game, at the prompt, or on the BBS.

dos-manuals.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at Owner’s Guide in the ⋯ menu
dos-manuals.text: The Owner’s Guide is Game-Maker’s manual. The Ultimate Guide has the advanced tips and tricks.

dos-menus.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the screen
dos-menus.text: Then its menus: Play runs a game in PLAYGAME, Design opens the tools that make one, Quit goes to DOS.

dos-power.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Power button
dos-power.text: Power switches it on and off. Off is really off: the next start is a fresh boot.

dos-prompt.text: At the DOS prompt, type GM to come back, or a game’s name on its disk to play it.

dos-reset.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at Reset in the ⋯ menu
dos-reset.text: Reset restarts the PC, like the button on the front of the case.

dos-sound.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Sound button
dos-sound.text: Sound switches the PC’s sound on and off.

dos-switch.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Desk, DOS and Web switch
dos-switch.text: Desk takes you back to the room around this PC, and Web to today’s site.

dos-turbo.where: DOS: Professor Fiddlesticks points at the Turbo button
dos-turbo.text: Turbo is sixty-six megahertz of pure speed. Off, it plods along like an old 286.

editor-assistant.where: Editor: Watt points at the Assistant button
editor-assistant.text: The Assistant lets your own AI look at a game and change it with you. Set it up in Settings first.

editor-blocks.where: Editor: Watt points at the Blocks list
editor-blocks.text: Pick a block from this list…

editor-building.where: Editor: Watt points at the Building tool
editor-building.text: Building drags out a whole house, any size, from its parts.

editor-bye.where: Editor: Watt says goodbye and walks off
editor-bye.text: Time to recharge. Happy making! Beep.

editor-check.where: Editor: Watt points at the Level check panel
editor-check.text: The Level check lets a bot play the level, then shows where it went and what players might mind.

editor-copy.where: Editor: Watt points at the Edit a copy button
editor-copy.text: Ready to make it yours? Edit a copy, and start changing things.

editor-files.where: Editor: Watt points at the list of the game’s files
editor-files.text: Every file in the game, sorted by kind: palettes, blocks, monsters, maps, music and more.

editor-hello.text: Beep! Watt here, from Ohm Sweet Ohm. This is the editor, open on my game just as it shipped.

editor-level.where: Editor: Watt points at the Play Level button
editor-level.text: Play Level jumps straight into a level. The arrow beside it picks which one, and where to start.

editor-links.where: Editor: Watt points at the Links button
editor-links.text: Links shows the doors: gold marks are exits to other scenes, cyan marks are where the hero comes in.

editor-map.where: Editor: Watt points at the map’s name
editor-map.text: This is a map: one level, laid out in blocks, a hundred by a hundred.

editor-monsters.where: Editor: Watt points at the Monsters tool
editor-monsters.text: Monsters puts the game’s creatures on the map. A right-click takes one away.

editor-paint.where: Editor: Watt points at the Paint tool
editor-paint.text: …then paint with it. Line, Rectangle and Fill lay down lots at once.

editor-palette.where: Editor: Watt points at the note about color 0
editor-palette.text: In a palette, mind color 0: the game draws its menus and text screens on it. Press backgrounds to see them.

editor-play.where: Editor: Watt points at the Play Game button
editor-play.text: Play Game plays it from its title screen, right here, without leaving the editor.

editor-readonly.where: Editor: Watt points at the Read-only bar
editor-readonly.text: Looking inside changes nothing. Edit a copy makes your own copy of the game to change.

editor-terrain.where: Editor: Watt points at the Terrain tool
editor-terrain.text: Terrain paints grass, water or paths, and chooses the edges and corners for you.

guide-bye.where: Guide: Inspector Penn says goodbye and walks off
guide-bye.text: Case closed. When you’re stuck, the answer is usually in here.

guide-contents.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at The editors in the Guide’s contents
guide-contents.text: The contents, one part at a time. The editors explains each tool, from maps to music.

guide-hello.text: Inspector Ada Penn. Every case needs a good guide, and so does making games. This is it.

guide-home.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at The home page heading
guide-home.text: Here, the home page: making a new game, bringing one in, and every shelf of games.

guide-next.where: Guide: Inspector Penn presses the next part’s link
guide-next.text: At the bottom, the next part’s name takes you on. One clue at a time.

guide-owners.where: Guide: Inspector Penn presses the Open the Owner’s Guide button
guide-owners.text: The Owner’s Guide explains every part of a game, and how the parts fit together.

guide-owners-page.where: Guide: Inspector Penn presses the Owner’s Guide’s next page arrow
guide-owners-page.text: It opens in the Game-Maker box, as it came in 1994. Turn the pages, or print it as a booklet.

guide-sharing.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at Sharing your game in the Guide’s contents
guide-sharing.text: Sharing your game: a web app for any web host, a copy for real DOS, or just its files.

guide-start.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at the Getting started heading
guide-start.text: Getting started: how to design, play and share games in this web version.

guide-tip.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at the tip for new game makers
guide-tip.text: New here? Play a game, Look inside it, Edit a copy, then change one small thing and play again.

guide-ultimate.where: Guide: Inspector Penn presses the Open The Ultimate Owner’s Guide button
guide-ultimate.text: The Ultimate Owner’s Guide is about making a game people enjoy. The Level check uses its checklists.

guide-ultimate-read.where: Guide: Inspector Penn points at The Ultimate Owner’s Guide, open
guide-ultimate-read.text: Heroes that feel right, levels that teach, fair enemies, then play-testing. A case file for every game.

home-achievements.where: Home: Teddy points at Achievements in the header
home-achievements.text: Achievements keeps track of what you’ve done, here and on the 1994 desk.

home-another.where: Home: Teddy presses the Another button
home-another.text: Another picks a different game at random. Ooh, good one.

home-bye.where: Home: Gwinn says goodbye and walks off
home-bye.text: That’s the tour! Now go play something.

home-cast.where: Home: Teddy points at Cast in the header
home-cast.text: The Cast page is where you meet Teddy, me, and everyone else from the new games.

home-download.where: Home: Teddy points at the Download button
home-download.text: Download makes a copy to play on Windows, a Mac, Linux, the web, or real DOS.

home-games.where: Home: Teddy points at Games in the header
home-games.text: Games, up in the bar, always brings you back here.

home-guide.where: Home: Teddy points at Guide in the header
home-guide.text: The Guide explains making games, one part at a time.

home-guides.where: Home: Teddy points at the ? Guides button
home-guides.text: Press this button any time to see this tour again, or to have Teddy and me wait on a page for you.

home-hello.text: Hi! I’m Gwinn. This little guy is my brother Teddy. He and I will show you around.

home-imported-none.where: Home: Teddy points at the import tile
home-imported-none.text: Nothing here yet? Drop game files on this tile, or click it to pick them.

home-library.where: Home: Teddy points at Library in the header
home-library.text: The Library has things to read and print: manuals, maps, sticker sheets and a magazine.

home-look.where: Home: Teddy points at the Look inside button
home-look.text: Look inside opens its files in the editor, just as they shipped. Change something and you get a copy of your own.

home-new.where: Home: Teddy presses the New game button
home-new.text: New game starts one of your own: ready to play, empty, or described in words for your own AI to build.

home-note.where: Home: Teddy points at the Add a note button
home-note.text: Add a note keeps a few words about a game, just for you.

home-notes-search.where: Home: Teddy points at the Find a game box
home-notes-search.text: And the search box finds the words in your notes, too.

home-offline.where: Home: Teddy points at Play offline in the Settings menu
home-offline.text: Settings has Play offline, which saves the whole site so it works with no connection.

home-play.where: Home: Teddy presses the Play button
home-play.text: Play starts it right here in your browser, with the keyboard or a gamepad.

home-rate.where: Home: Teddy points at the rating stars of the imported game up top
home-rate.text: Up top is one of them. Give it one to five stars: your rating saves at once.

home-search.where: Home: Teddy points at the Find a game box
home-search.text: Looking for one game? Type part of its name here.

home-shareware-notice.where: Home: Teddy points at the shareware games
home-shareware-notice.text: They’re other people’s games, so most just play here, exactly as released. Each keeps its author’s notice.

home-shareware-what.where: Home: Teddy points at the shareware games
home-shareware-what.text: Shareware meant try it free. If you kept playing, you sent the author a fee. Games got around on floppy disks and BBSes.

home-show.where: Home: Teddy points at the Show rating picker
home-show.text: Show narrows the list to one rating, or to the games you haven’t rated yet.

home-showcase.where: Home: Teddy points at the big game picture at the top
home-showcase.text: Up top is one game, shown big. Its picture plays a short demo of the game.

home-sort.where: Home: Teddy points at the Sort by picker
home-sort.text: Sort by Rating puts your five-star games first, with the unrated ones last.

home-stars.where: Home: Teddy points at a rated tile’s stars
home-stars.text: Rated games wear their stars on their tiles.

home-tab-bizarre.where: Home: Teddy presses the Bizarre tab
home-tab-bizarre.text: Bizarre: big, heartfelt songs about all the wrong things, each one made into a game.

home-tab-gameware.where: Home: Teddy presses the Gameware tab
home-tab-gameware.text: Gameware: the free games that came with Game-Maker. Play one, or edit a copy to see how it works.

home-tab-imported.where: Home: Teddy presses the Imported tab
home-tab-imported.text: Imported holds games you bring in: a folder, some files, a .zip, or a one-page export.

home-tab-mine.where: Home: Teddy presses the My games tab
home-tab-mine.text: My games: the ones you make here, or copy from a shelf to change. They stay in this browser.

home-tab-sandbox.where: Home: Teddy presses the Sandbox tab
home-tab-sandbox.text: Sandbox: new games made with Game-Maker in its original formats, so they play in real DOS too.

home-tab-shareware.where: Home: Teddy presses the Shareware tab
home-tab-shareware.text: Shareware: games other people made with Game-Maker, from the CD and the BBSes.

home-tabs.where: Home: Teddy points at the collection tabs
home-tabs.text: These tabs are the collections: your games, ones you bring in, and shelves of games ready to play.

home-theme.where: Home: Teddy points at Theme in the Settings menu
home-theme.text: Theme switches between dark, light, or whatever your computer uses.

home-tiles.where: Home: Teddy presses a game tile
home-tiles.text: Pick any tile and its game moves up top.

home-views.where: Home: Teddy points at the Desk, DOS and Web switch
home-views.text: Desk, DOS and Web: a 1994 desk with its PC, DOS Game-Maker on its own, or this page.

home-walkthrough.where: Home: Teddy points at the Walkthrough button
home-walkthrough.text: Stuck? Walkthrough plays the whole game for you, start to finish.

library-all.where: Library: Lewie presses the All games button
library-all.text: Showing just one game? This puts everything back on the shelves.

library-bye.where: Library: Joe says goodbye and walks off
library-bye.text: Please return every word to its book. Exactly one hundred at a time.

library-card.where: Library: Lewie points at the first manual on the shelves
library-card.text: Each card opens its piece on screen: a manual, a hint book, a map, a key card. Most can be printed, too.

library-count.where: Library: Joe points at the count of things on the shelves
library-count.text: This counts everything on the shelves. I counted them too. Twice.

library-guide.where: Library: Lewie points at the Guide card
library-guide.text: The Guide and the help for Mac, Windows and Linux are shelved here as well.

library-hello.text: Good evening. I’m Joe, the night librarian. Everything on these shelves is to read, print or watch.

library-lewie.text: Hi, I’m Lewie! I shoveled a lot of snow to buy Game-Maker. All the paper from the game boxes is here.

library-magazine.where: Library: Lewie points at the TURBO BUTTON card
library-magazine.text: TURBO BUTTON is the shareware gamer’s monthly: news, reviews, hints and every game.

library-pick.where: Library: Lewie points at the Game or Kind picker
library-pick.text: Pick one game, or one kind, to see just that shelf.

library-print.where: Library: Lewie points at a Disk labels card
library-print.text: Disk labels and retail boxes open in the print shop, with lines to cut and fold along.

library-sort.where: Library: Lewie points at the By game and By type buttons
library-sort.text: Sort the shelves by game, or by type: every manual together, every map together.

library-walkthrough.where: Library: Lewie points at a Walkthrough card
library-walkthrough.text: Every game’s walkthrough is here too, played start to finish. Its length is on the card.

settings-ai.where: Settings: Max points at AI setup in the Settings menu
settings-ai.text: AI setup connects your own AI, on your computer or with your own key, for the editor’s Assistant.

settings-backup.where: Settings: Max points at Back up / restore in the Settings menu
settings-backup.text: Back up saves everything this browser keeps to one file. Restore brings it back, here or on another computer.

settings-bye.where: Settings: Max says goodbye and walks off
settings-bye.text: Delivered. Signed, sealed, and on to the next world.

settings-credits.where: Settings: Max points at Credits in the Settings menu
settings-credits.text: Credits names who and what made everything here. That’s this page.

settings-hello.text: Courier Max, with a delivery: the settings. They live behind the gear, top right.

settings-offline.where: Settings: Max points at Play offline in the Settings menu
settings-offline.text: Play offline says how big the whole site is, then saves it all, so it works with no connection.

settings-page.where: Settings: Max points at the Credits page’s sections
settings-page.text: This page’s sections: the people who made the original Game-Maker, the game authors, and every tool used, AI too.

settings-source.where: Settings: Max points at Source on GitHub in the Settings menu
settings-source.text: Source on GitHub: every line of this site’s code, open for anyone to read.

settings-theme.where: Settings: Max points at Theme in the Settings menu
settings-theme.text: Theme goes dark, light, or whatever your computer uses. Each press picks the next one.

settings-tour.where: Settings: Max points at Guided tour in the Settings menu
settings-tour.text: Guided tour plays this whole tour again, every page in order.
